B = "/Users/kristinarash/Library/Caches/sportsci-batch-100"

def load(i):
    return json.load(open(f"{B}/drafts/{i}.json"))

def save(i, d):
    with open(f"{B}/verified/{i}.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(d, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)

# ---- Q04 / Q05 (same article, AAM and published version) ----
for i, other in (("Q04", "Q05"), ("Q05", "Q04")):
    d = load(i)
    d["screeningLimitations"] = ("Injury and performance data come from public sources with no clinical detail, so injury severity and diagnosis are unknown and hip and core injuries are grouped broadly. "
        "Power ratings are composite measures that exclude linemen and kickers, and some abstract and discussion claims (offensive players playing fewer games after core than hip injury, and fewer than controls after core injury) have no supporting test in the results tables.")
    d["synthesisCaution"] = ("Staff could read the within-player pre-to-post drops in games and power rating as an injury effect, when the only significant difference from matched controls was fewer games played by defensive players in the two years after injury (9.5 vs 10.9).")
    p = d["paper"]
    p["findings"] = ("All injured players returned to play, with offensive and defensive players missing 4.0 and 3.1 games on average. "
        "Defensive players played fewer career games after versus before injury (37.4 vs 58.1, p < 0.01) and had lower power ratings (133.9 vs 219.8, p < 0.01), and two years after injury they played fewer games than controls (9.5 vs 10.9, p = 0.04), but cumulative post-injury games and power ratings did not differ from controls. "
        "The offensive skill-player power rating fell after injury (341.8 to 205.7, p = 0.03) while controls showed no change, with no significant difference between injured players and controls.")
    p["limitations"] = ("Injury data come from public reports with no clinical detail, and the hip and core injury groups are broad. "
        "Power ratings exclude linemen and kickers, and the abstract and discussion state that offensive players played fewer games after core injury (versus hip injury and versus controls) without a matching result in the tables; the defensive power rating SD also differs between text and table (128.8 vs 128.5). "
        "The design has no randomisation and cannot show that the injury caused the changes.")
    p["practicalImplications"] = ("Staff can expect NFL players with non-operatively managed hip or core injuries to return to play, most within the same season, after missing about 3 to 4 games. "
        "Defensive players played slightly fewer games than matched controls over the next two seasons (9.5 vs 10.9), but cumulative post-injury games and power ratings did not differ from controls.")
    p["athleteDev"] = ("The study suggests return to competition is likely after a non-operative hip or core injury, but it covers only NFL players and does not measure development, training or skill outcomes, so it cannot guide training progression.")
    d["verification"] = {
        "status": "CORRECTED",
        "changes": [
            "practicalImplications: said defensive players were 'missing more games for about two seasons' (defenders actually missed fewer games at injury, 3.1 vs 4.0) -> now states slightly fewer games than controls over two seasons ('9.5 ± 7.0 versus 10.9 ± 6.8, p<0.05')",
            "synthasisCaution/synthesisCaution: claimed no uninjured comparison for the pre-to-post decline, but offensive controls were compared ('control players demonstrated no difference (350 ± 708.9 vs 335 ± 680.5; p=0.38)') -> reframed around the single significant between-group result",
            "screeningLimitations and limitations: vague 'offensive subgroup power rating values' discrepancy replaced with the real problem, abstract/discussion claims about offensive core injuries ('played fewer cumulative career games returning from core injury versus hip') with no supporting test in the results",
            "findings: added p < 0.01 for defensive power rating and noted offensive controls showed no change",
            "athleteDev: removed 'developing players' framing; sample is NFL players only"
        ],
        "residualConcerns": f"Same article and DOI as {other} ({'accepted author manuscript' if i=='Q04' else 'published version'} here); keep only one record in the library. Abstract and discussion include claims about offensive core injuries not supported by the reported tables.",
        "spotCheckPriority": "high"
    }
    d["verification"]["changes"][1] = d["verification"]["changes"][1].replace("synthasisCaution/", "")
    save(i, d)

# ---- Q06 ----
d = load("Q06")
d["verification"] = {
    "status": "VERIFIED",
    "changes": [],
    "residualConcerns": "",
    "spotCheckPriority": "normal"
}
save("Q06", d)

# ---- Q07 ----
d = load("Q07")
d["screeningLimitations"] = ("The sample is 12 recreational lifters, the test is a Smith machine bench press with bench press throws, and the authors note that between-session reliability was not assessed. "
    "The best model under-predicted 1RM by about 9 kg with a significant difference from the measured value (P < 0.001), and predicting 1RM means extrapolating beyond the tested loads, which the authors say severely compromises accuracy.")
p = d["paper"]
p["limitations"] = ("Only 12 recreational lifters were tested, the velocity data came from a single session, and between-session reliability was not assessed. "
    "The test was done only on a Smith machine bench press with bench press throws, so results may not transfer to free-weight lifting or other exercises. "
    "The 1RM is extrapolated beyond the tested load range, which the authors note compromises accuracy, and the best model under-predicted 1RM.")
p["practicalImplications"] = ("Practitioners testing recreational lifters on a Smith machine could use three bench press throws at 30, 40 and 50% of an estimated 1RM, with peak bar velocity, to get a rough 1RM estimate and a training load reference. "
    "Because the model under-predicted by about 9 kg, the estimate should be treated as approximate.")
p["athleteDev"] = ("Light-load bench press throw testing could give a rough 1RM estimate for athletes new to lifting without near-maximal lifts. "
    "The study did not test whether the method tracks strength change over time, and its accuracy for youth or trained athletes is unknown.")
d["verification"] = {
    "status": "CORRECTED",
    "changes": [
        "screeningLimitations and limitations: said the model 'was tested only within the load range it was built from', which is backwards; 1RM prediction extrapolates beyond the tested loads ('the accuracy of regression models that attempt to predict values outside of the range of the collected data is severely compromised')",
        "limitations: 'tested in one session' -> two sessions (1RM, then BP-T 2-3 days later); velocity data from a single session",
        "athleteDev: removed claim that the method can 'track strength changes'; no longitudinal test was done",
        "practicalImplications: added Smith machine context and removed 'rechecked over time' advice not tested"
    ],
    "residualConcerns": "",
    "spotCheckPriority": "normal"
}
save("Q07", d)

# ---- Q08 ----
d = load("Q08")
d["screeningLimitations"] = ("No search strategy or appraisal of the studies cited is described, and recommendations mix cited studies with the authors' experience; most underlying load-velocity research uses barbell lifts, often on Smith machines. "
    "The worked examples come from single individuals, and the abstract names injury prevention as an aim without evidence for it in the text.")
p = d["paper"]
p["tldr"] = ("Velocity-based training uses bar speed to set and check loads, so training can match each athlete's daily capacity. "
    "For team sports, the authors recommend individual load-velocity profiles, consistent validated devices, and repetitions in reserve for exercises without velocity tracking.")
p["limitations"] = ("The paper does not describe how sources were selected or appraised, and it presents no new data. "
    "Recommendations are largely expert-based and the examples are individual cases; the velocity-loss thresholds come from cited studies, while the R2 cut-off of 0.92 is stated as the authors' experience. "
    "Injury prevention is named as an aim without supporting evidence in the text.")
p["rtp"] = ("The paper mentions return to play only in passing in its introduction and offers no return-to-play protocol or evidence. "
    "It cannot be used to decide when an injured athlete is ready to load or return to sport.")
d["verification"] = {
    "status": "CORRECTED",
    "changes": [
        "rtp: removed unsupported suggestion that velocity monitoring could be part of a return-to-training plan; the text only cites RT importance for return to play in the introduction",
        "limitations: velocity-loss thresholds are cited work ('Studies have observed that low velocity loss thresholds (i.e., 10-20% loss...)'), only the R2 0.92 cut-off is 'in our experience'",
        "screeningLimitations: 'most recommendations rest on the authors' experience' -> recommendations mix cited studies and experience",
        "tldr: framed recommendations as the authors' rather than established findings"
    ],
    "residualConcerns": "",
    "spotCheckPriority": "normal"
}
save("Q08", d)
print("ok")
